Longitudinal studies would also help determine whether users maintain the same boundaries around AI authority after experiencing successful delegation, system failures, or changes in trust over time.

6. Conclusion

AI agents are increasingly capable of acting on users’ behalf across a wide range of everyday and work activities, but willingness to delegate is highly task dependent. Through an online survey that collected responses from 289 U.S. adults across 45 scenarios spanning nine life domains, we found that automation preferences varied substantially by domain. Greater trust in the AI, desired AI leadership, prior task-specific AI use, and anticipated financial savings were associated with greater automation preference, whereas concern about losing personal fulfillment was associated with lower automation preference. Privacy concern also varied across domains, but it did not independently predict automation preference after adjustment. Our findings further show that delegation is not well captured by a single continuum from human performance to full automation. Participants distinguished among how much of a task the AI should execute, how much collaboration they wanted, how much leadership the AI should hold, and where human authority should remain. Qualitative analysis on open-ended responses revealed a preference for bounded autonomy, in which AI could perform substantial portions of a task while humans retained oversight, approval, or final decision authority. These results suggest that the design of agentic AI should focus not only on increasing capability, but also on configuring the boundaries of delegation. Systems that allow users to separately control execution, collaboration, leadership, and authority may better reflect how people want responsibility to be distributed between themselves and increasingly autonomous AI agents.

Appendix A Study Protocol and Survey Instrument

Items are presented in their administered order. For readability, item labels in this document have been reassigned to reflect presentation order rather than Qualtrics’ internal question IDs. Original Qualtrics IDs for the renumbered items are provided in the item-ID mapping table at the end of this document. Conditional display logic is stated immediately above the item it governs.

A.1. Survey Flow

A screening branch terminated the survey for respondents who declined consent. Within each of the nine scenario blocks, the Qualtrics Loop & Merge and Randomizer functionalities selected one of five candidate scenarios with equal probability, independently across blocks. All nine scenario blocks administered an identical battery in identical order.

A.2. Consent

C1. Welcome!

You are being asked to participate in a voluntary research study. The purpose of this study is to understand how individuals integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents into daily routines, and their attitudes toward expanded automation and augmentation by AI systems. Your participation is expected to last approximately thirty minutes. The risks associated with this research are minimal, and are no greater than those you ordinarily encounter in your daily activities. The benefits of participating in this research include contributing to a broader understanding of how AI technologies are used in everyday life and decision-making, while informing the development of AI agents that align with user needs and desires.

We invite you to take part in the research study because you are currently living in the United States, are older than 18 years of age, and have previously used AI agents. If you complete this research study, and your responses are deemed as legitimate (not generated by a Large Language Model or AI) by the research team, you will receive $10 in the form of an Amazon gift card for your time and effort.

If you have questions, concerns, complaints, or think the research has harmed you, you may talk to the research team at [redacted for review]. This research is being overseen by an Institutional Review Board (“IRB”). You may also contact them at [redacted for review] if you have questions regarding your rights as a research participant or other questions, concerns, or complaints.

By clicking the button below, you acknowledge that your participation in the study is voluntary, you are 18 years of age, and that you are aware that you may choose to terminate your participation in the study at any time and for any reason.

Please note that this survey will be best displayed on a laptop or desktop computer. Some features may be less compatible for use on a mobile device.

A.8. Scenario Descriptions

Tables 3 and 4 reproduce the task summary and task description exactly as shown to participants, for all 45 scenarios. The # column gives the Loop & Merge row index, which corresponds to the loop-iteration prefix on the exported response columns. Each scenario was additionally accompanied by an AI-generated illustration of the activity; the illustration files are omitted here.

A.9. Scenario Illustration Generation

Each of the 45 scenarios was accompanied by an AI-generated illustration intended to help participants visualize the activity being evaluated. The illustrations depicted the activity itself rather than a particular AI agent, interface, or embodiment.

The illustrations were generated using a common prompt structure with Gemini Nano Banana 2. Based on the retained generation prompts, prompts followed the form:

Generate a realistic image of the daily task of [task-specific activity description]. Do not include a person in the image.

Only the task-specific activity description varied across scenarios. Examples of retained prompts include:

  • •

    Recipe Search and Creation: Generate a realistic image of the daily task of searching for and creating recipes based on available ingredients and dietary preferences. Do not include a person in the image.

  • •

    Home Systems Adjustment: Generate a realistic image of the daily task of adjusting a home’s lighting, temperature, and energy settings. Do not include a person in the image.

  • •

    Home Improvement Guidance: Generate a realistic image of the daily task of following instructions for minor home repairs and improvements. Do not include a person in the image.

  • •

    Home Safety Monitoring: Generate a realistic image of the daily task of monitoring a home for safety hazards such as gas leaks, fires, or intrusions. Do not include a person in the image.

  • •

    Entertainment Recommendation: Generate a realistic image of the daily task of browsing and selecting music, movies, or TV content based on personal preferences. Do not include a person in the image.

For each scenario, the first generated image that did not contain obvious visual defects or a substantial mismatch with the intended task was retained. Participants were informed that the illustrations were AI-generated and did not depict real people or events.

A.10. Item-ID Mapping

Table 5 maps the reader-facing item labels used in this supplementary document to the original Qualtrics question IDs. The 23-item scenario evaluation battery retains the sequential item numbering used throughout this document.

A.11. De-identification

Direct identifiers removed from the analytic datasets prior to analysis included IP addresses, gift-card email addresses, recruitment-platform identifiers, and geolocation information. Respondent identifiers retained for analysis were de-identified internal IDs.
